courses.subject: POPG
courses.title: Health of Remote and Displaced Populations
courses.description: This module examines the several aspects relating to rural and remote health such as inequity and inaccessibility to healthcare; ethnic minority and indigenous health; cases studies of rural and remote health programmes in low, middle and high income countries.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:
1. gain awareness of issues in rural and remote health
2. understand major measurements of the rural health of population and its determinants
3. have the ability to interpret the reasons for rural health variations of the world and its nations
courses.course_syllabus:
| **Topic** | **Content** |
| --- | --- |
| Overview Needs assessment of rural communities | Characteristics of rural and remote health. Methods of community needs assessment |
| Ethnic minorities and Indigenous health 1 | Ethnic & indigenous health Cultural awareness, cultural sensitivity, cultural competence |
| Ethnic minorities and Indigenous health 2 | Ethnic & indigenous health |
| Primary Care | Rural Primary Health Care. Human resources for health: retention of rural health care workers |
| Maternal & Child Health | Pilot programme design. Maternal health in rural China. IMCI. Malnutrition. |
| Working and living in rural & remote areas in real life | Practicalities and tips for rural field work |
| 1. Water, sanitation and hygiene 2. Cook stove and indoor air pollution | Water safety and sanitation. Cooking fuel and indoor air pollution. |
| Rural & remote health systems | Case studies of rural health systems globally |

2. Strasser R. **Rural health around the world: challenges and solutions**. Family Practice 2003; 20:457–463.

courses.subject: POPG
courses.title: Global Reproductive Health
courses.description: The purpose of this class is to examine reproductive health issues, services, programs, and policies from an international perspective. The course content will include social, environmental, economic, behavioral, and political factors that affect fertility, and pregnancy outcome, reproductive health, and family planning in developed and developing countries. The course will have four areas of focus: (1) reproductive health issues and trends; (2) interventions and programs to improve reproductive health; (3) measurement and interpretation of reproductive indices; (4) policies that affect reproductive health and health care provision.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
For TPg student under School of Public Health:
- Master of Public Health / Postgraduate Diploma in Public Health;- MSc/PgD in Epidemiology and Biostatistics;- MSc/PgD in Health Services Management.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:
1. Understand the terminology and vocabulary used in the reproductive literature.
2. Identify the major governmental and non-governmental agencies that make global health policy.
3. Identify trends in reproductive health relative to economic, demographic, and environmental changes in various regions of the world
4. Describe the factors that contribute to effective interventions to improve the reproductive health of adolescents, men, and women and how “effective” interventions vary according to political, social, cultural, and economic realities.
5. Develop a public health perspective towards service provision and policy for reproductive health issues

courses.subject: POPG
courses.title: Disaster and Humanitarian Crisis
courses.description: Disaster and humanitarian responses are crucial elements in public health practices. Humanitarian relief actions often highlight the importance of mitigation, preparedness, training and multidisciplinary collaborative response within and beyond the health and medical sector. This course offers an overview of the disaster management cycle and the public health and medical implications of disaster and humanitarian crisis. It aims to show how public health principles may be applied in disaster relief and how evidence-based health related humanitarian actions can be planned, implemented and evaluated.

courses.subject: POPG
courses.title: Demography and Health
courses.description: A survey course on demographic methods for application to public health. The course will survey methods in fertility, mortality and migration analysis to assist future global health workers in population policy. Demographic modeling and software will be introduced
courses.enrollment_requirement:
For TPg student under School of Public Health:
- Master of Public Health;- MSc/PgD in Epidemiology & Biostatistics; - MSc/PgD in Health Services Management;- PgD in Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, student should be able to:
1. describe the basic concepts of health demography from three perspectives (demographic, epidemiologic and social science)
2. describe the relationship among health, healthcare and demography
3. define and measure population size, distribution, concentration and their trends, and their implications for health, healthcare and policies
4. Understand the different ways to display and analyze compositional variables, and their implications for health, healthcare and policies
5. describe the concepts and measures behind the three most important elements of demography: mortality, fertility and migration (as well as morbidity)
6. describe different data collection methods, data sources for health demography studies
7. describe, assess and evaluate the demographic correlates of health status and health behavior
courses.course_syllabus:
| Health Demography: An Introduction Class Exercise |
| --- |
| Population Size, Distribution, Concentration and Composition Class Exercise |
| Fertility Class Exercise |
| Migration Class Exercise |
| Mortality Class Exercise |
| Morbidity Class Exercise |
| Data Collection and Demographic Correlates of Health Status, Health Behavior Class Exercise |
courses.required_readings: Pol LG, Thomas RK. The Demography of Health and Healthcare. 3rd edition. Springer: 2013 (E-book). URL: <http://link.springer.com/book/10.1007%2F978-90-481-8903-8>

courses.subject: POPG
courses.title: Global Health Perspectives of Humanitarian Crisis and Human Security
courses.description: Human security is an emerging paradigm in the global healthcare community that can be applied to guide local and global public health practices. It can also provide a basis to link up related themes under the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Through various real-life case studies and practical applications, this course will provide participants with an understanding of how the human security and health security concepts are applied in public health practices, especially under emergencies and disasters. The challenges with putting the human security concept into operation will also be explored.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this module, students are expected to be able to:
- Describe and explain the principles of humanitarian and human security and how they impact health access
and outcomes
- Understand the current state of human security and how it affects global health inequalities
- Apply human-security frameworks, tools and methods to participants’ fields of practice
- Discuss the impact of forced migration due to conflict and disaster
- Acknowledge the breadth the of the study of humanitarian issues
- Self-reflect on the importance of addressing humanitarian issues in the contemporary world

| Global Migration |

| Research methods and application in emergencies |

courses.subject: POPG
courses.title: Field Action Lab
courses.description: This is a practicum course aims at providing a unique opportunity for students to gain familiarity with public health practice. Practicum experience allows students to integrate and apply the knowledge and skills they learned through coursework and prior experiences in a public health environment. Students are required to complete an approved public health practice related practicum (single or combined experience) in a variety of settings, including rural field trip, governmental and non-governmental health agencies, academic institutions, or community settings under the supervision of site administrators (mentors/ practicum supervisors) and the guidance from the School of Public Health and Primary Care. Students will be involved in project planning, field-based health needs assessment, health intervention, project evaluation and report writing during the field practicum.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to:
1. gain familiarity with public health practices in programs planning, policies, and service delivery settings.
2. apply public health theories and concepts into practices in the community
3. use it as a recommended background course for practices-based Capstone.
courses.course_syllabus:
| Introduction of field action laboratory. Project planning and evaluation |
| --- |
| Introduction of potential field sites |
| Field project management |
| Medical and health aspects of field based project & Humanitarian operations |
| Guidelines writing and review reports |
